content:
Whitney's reference leads with objections wedding pros voice, such as ads feeling generic, wanting aligned leads, and wanting confidence in the investment. It positions WIA as intentional, brand-aligned, and ROI-focused, as opposed to agencies that promise leads without understanding positioning or buyer psychology.

Candidate A names the problem less directly. It opens with a general line about marketing and then explains the Google and Meta strategy. It adds a specific result ("$90,000 in booked revenue from ads in 90 days, with 59 leads and 9 bookings"), which was not provided in the request, so it may be fabricated or unverifiable. That is a significant accuracy risk. It also covers trust, transparency, and the managed or DIY options, and it ends with the CTA. Its tone is measured and fits the reference.

Candidate B opens on the problem (bookings depending on being found) and addresses quality inquiries over lead volume, which matches the research. It does not invent a specific figure, but it does claim "double their business, grow their teams," which is also unsupported by the request. It covers trust and support, the managed or DIY options, and "you don't need to know which platform is right," which addresses the "not sure ads are right" objection. The CTA is clear. It uses bold formatting and is somewhat longer, but it is closer to the reference's themes of quality inquiries, not treating everyone the same, and confidence.

Both include unsupported claims. A's is a specific invented case study with exact numbers, which is riskier and harder to edit around. B's is vaguer but still unsupported, and is easier to remove. B better addresses the research objections and the problem WIA solves, so it needs fewer edits.

{"winner": "B", "edits_needed_A": "some", "edits_needed_B": "few", "reason": "B opens on the problem, centers quality inquiries over lead volume, and answers the research objections (trust, unsure about ads) in a way close to the reference. A fabricates a specific $90,000/59 leads/9 bookings case study that would have to be verified or removed, and it is less focused on the problem. B's 'double their business' claim is also unsup

request.system:
You compare two draft pieces of marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), a wedding-industry advertising agency. You are given the request, the version WIA's co-founder Whitney actually approved or wrote (the reference), and two candidate drafts. Decide which candidate would need fewer and smaller edits to become something Whitney would approve. Judge substance first (what is claimed, for whom, how WIA is positioned, accuracy, whether her own wording was kept where she supplied it), then voice. Do not reward length, and do not require the candidate to copy the reference wording.

Return only JSON: {"winner": "A" or "B" or "tie", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "one or two sentences"} where edits_needed values are none, few, some or many.

Request:
Below is the transcript of a reel I'm going to post tomorrow. I need a caption to go along with it. 

It needs to appeal to venues/wedding pros who want consistent lead generation and profitable ads (regardless of if they would be a better fit for Elevate or the Accelerators)

It should be able to take someone from cold to sold

Be sure to highlight the problem Wedding Industry Ads solves for our clients and the fact that they get amazing results

From recent market research, most respondents said that their biggest problem before working with us wasn't getting in front of enough clients consistently. One said finding a marketing approach that felt aligned with her brand and sustainable long-term. Another said finding a marketing strategy that will actually work.

What's most important to them about making an investment like this was split evenly between:
-feeling supported, confident and guided in the team they're working with
-having a clear strategy and confidence investment will generate strong return
-seeing efficient progress and knowing I'm making a smart move for my business

Most said that what would hold them back is:
"I'd want to be confident the strategy will actually bring in quality inquiries, not just more leads"
Another said they've hear of horror stories investing in agencies and would need to trust the team
And one said she isn't 100% sure if paid ads are right for her

CTA can be to visit our link in bio to learn about the ways they can work with us

Daniela: And to be fair, it's not that organic marketing doesn't have a place in 2026 or moving forward. It's that ads can help create more stability around lead generation specifically. And then that way when people do go over to your website or they do go over to your Instagram profile or whatever your social accounts are that you use, there's something relevant there for them to consume. But the point of entry is where you can control them.



Whitney: Yeah. And so we've got the points of entry on Google with Google search. We can run paid campaigns there, right? To make sure that you are showing up in the search results for the exact keywords that you want to be showing up for for couples who are searching with high intent. They want to find a venue or a vendor just like you. 



Daniela: People are booking wedding vendors from Google searches, but oftentimes when people are searching, they'll hit your website and then they might click away. They're researching a bunch of different options. And so that's where Meta can really support the Google ad campaigns as well. Then you can stay top of mind in the newsfeed. You can make sure that the people who have landed on your website, even if they're not following you, that they're able to consume the content that you're putting so much work into creating, right? And then they're able to keep you top of mind so they can book you when they're ready.

Reference (what Whitney approved):
One thing we hear often from wedding pros before they work with us is:

“I don’t want my ads to feel generic.”
“I want to know the leads coming in are actually aligned.”
“I just want to feel confident I’m making a smart investment.”

And honestly, that hesitation makes complete sense.

The wedding industry is full of agencies promising more leads without understanding positioning, buyer psychology, or what actually turns quality inquiries into booked clients.

Most business owners aren’t looking for flashy marketing.

They’re looking for a strategy that feels intentional, brand-aligned, and capable of generating real ROI long-term.

Candidate A:
You’ve put real work into building a business couples want to book. Your marketing should help more of the right couples find it, consistently.

That’s what we help venues and wedding pros do at Wedding Industry Ads.

We build Google and Meta ad strategies around how couples actually choose their wedding vendors: searching, comparing, revisiting, and getting comfortable enough to inquire.

Your brand, website, and organic content all have a role in that decision. Paid ads build on that foundation, creating more intentional opportunities for couples to discover you and stay connected while they decide.

And we look beyond the campaigns themselves. Your positioning, landing page, follow-up, and conversion tracking help turn that visibility into meaningful inquiries and bookings.

That combination gets results.

One of our clients generated $90,000 in booked revenue from ads in 90 days, with 59 leads and 9 bookings. A strong business foundation paired with the right ad strategy made those results possible.

Just as important is knowing you have a team you can trust along the way.

With us, you understand the strategy, what we’re measuring, and how those insights inform the next decision. You get guidance from specialists who understand weddings and care about what happens after someone clicks.

Whether you want a team to manage your ads or support launching campaigns you’ll learn to manage yourself, we have ways to help you build more consistent lead generation with a clear strategy behind it.

Visit the link in our bio to explore the ways you can work with us.

Candidate B:
Your next booking shouldn’t depend on whether a couple happens to find you.

You can have a beautiful brand, an excellent client experience, and an Instagram full of work you’re proud of—and still wonder where next month’s inquiries will come from.

That doesn’t mean your business needs more content. It may need a more intentional way to bring the right couples into it.

Organic marketing helps couples get to know you. Paid ads can help more of the right people discover you—and give them reasons to come back.

Google Search can put you in front of couples actively looking for a venue or service like yours. Meta can help you stay visible while they compare options and decide who to trust.

But visibility alone isn’t the goal.

**The goal is quality inquiries that turn into profitable bookings.**

That takes more than an ad campaign. Your messaging, landing page, and follow-up all need to help couples feel confident taking the next step.

That’s the problem we solve at Wedding Industry Ads: the gap between having a business couples would love and having a reliable system to help them find—and choose—it.

We’ve helped wedding businesses double their business, grow their teams, and feel more confident in the marketing supporting their growth.

Not by treating every wedding business the same. By understanding their goals, building a strategy around them, and looking beyond clicks to the sales conversations and bookings that matter.

Whether you want a team to manage your ads or guidance to learn how to manage them yourself, you deserve to understand the strategy—and feel supported by the people helping you put it into practice.

You don’t need to arrive knowing which platform or level of support is right for you.

**Visit the link in our bio to explore the ways to work with us and find the right fit for your business.**
